raw:
<plan>
twist: Instead of finding a peaceful morning meal, Violet walks straight into a calculated hazing or territorial block by second-year riders who view first-years as walking corpses.
distinct: Dain attempts to intervene with rigid, rule-bound authority that only makes the hostile second-years push harder against Violet, highlighting the friction between his protection and her need to stand on her own.
</plan>
<nar>
The heavy stone corridors of {{Basgiath War College|loc}} hum with the low, predatory murmur of hundreds of cadets moving between morning drills. 

Violet keeps her shoulders back, though every step on the cold flagstones sends a dull, familiar ache through the leather bindings wrapped tightly around her fragile joints. 

She navigates by instinct and the rich, heavy scent of roasting meat and stale rye, following the press of bodies toward {{The Mess Hall|loc}}.

Pushing through the heavy iron-banded oak doors brings a wall of noise and heat. 

The vast hall is packed with long wooden tables scarred by decades of spilled mead, knife-throwing, and bloody brawls. 

Cadets in black leather uniforms are packed shoulder-to-shoulder, shouting over one another, trading insults, and bolting down heavy rations. 

It is a place where weakness is cataloged instantly, and Violet, with her slight frame and the distinct metallic silver-white tips of her dark hair, draws immediate, appraising stares from the older cadets seated near the entrance.

Before she can reach the food service counter, a tall second-year with a jagged scar along his jawline steps directly into her path, blocking her way with deliberate insolence. 

"Watch it, scribe," he rasps, his eyes raking over her slight build with open contempt. "The parapet didn't finish you off, then? Must have been luck. Though you won't last the week once sparring starts."

Before Violet has to formulate a biting historical retort or maneuver around him, {{Dain Aetos|npc}} appears at her side, his expression locked into a severe, protective frown. 

He steps squarely between Violet and the second-year, his uniform immaculate, his posture radiating rigid authority.

"Step aside, Rorison," Dain says, his voice cold and clipped, carrying the effortless weight of a squad leader. "She's with me. Find someone else to harass before I report you for insubordination."

Rorison snorts, casting a final, dismissive look at Violet over Dain's shoulder before melting back into the crowd of cadets. 

Dain turns to Violet, his jaw tight as he looks down at her with a mixture of familiar fondness and deep, entrenched anxiety. 

"You shouldn't be wandering the halls alone yet, Violet," Dain murmurs, his tone softening only slightly as he checks her posture, looking for any sign of a stumble or a newly dislocated joint. "The second-years are looking for blood today. Grab what you need, but stay close to my squad."
</nar>

basgiath_war_college.name: Basgiath War College
basgiath_war_college.description: A colossal, ancient stone fortress carved directly into the rugged peaks of the Blackwood Mountains. It is divided into distinct, highly competitive quadrants, designed to forge the defenders of Navarre or kill them in the attempt.

the_outskirts.name: The Outskirts & Borders
the_outskirts.description: The treacherous mountainous terrain surrounding the college and the wider, ward-protected kingdom of Navarre, where the illusion of safety begins to wear thin.

Violet's analytical gaze sweeps past the shouting clusters of cadets, ignoring the heavy platters of meat and the jeers echoing across the mess hall. 

Her mind maps the architectural layout of {{Basgiath War College|loc}}—retrieving the structural blueprints she had memorized from the Scribe archives years ago. 

She slips away from Dain's protective perimeter while his attention is briefly snagged by an incoming group of brawling third-years.

Weaving silently through the press of bodies, Violet ducks out of a side exit and rounds the damp stone exterior of the [[Cadet Barracks|loc]]. 

Half-hidden behind an overgrown ivy trellis sits a narrow, iron-strapped door, rusted shut at the hinges and entirely ignored by the passing patrols. 

She throws her weight against the iron ring, her shoulder jarring uncomfortably, and manages to pop the swollen timber frame inward with a dry crack of splintering wood.

A draft of freezing, subterranean air rushes up the stone stairwell, carrying the metallic tang of damp earth and old blood. 

Dain catches sight of her movement just as the door gives way, his boots ringing sharply against the cobbles as he strides after her. 

"Violet, stop—what are you doing?" Dain demands, reaching out a gloved hand to grab her arm before she can descend into the dark. 

"There are second-years waiting for me in every corridor, Dain," Violet retorts, slipping past his reach with a sharp twist of her hips. 'And I need somewhere I can breathe without someone trying to snap my spine.'

She descends into the gloom before he can haul her back, her fingers trailing along the damp stone wall to steady her fragile joints as the heavy oak door creaks shut above, plunging them into sudden, echoing silence.

<plan>
twist: the cellar isn't actually empty; someone important from the rebellion or command uses it in secret, making it a dangerous discovery instead of a safe hideout.
distinct: Dain immediately tries to pull Violet away from it based on his strict adherence to regulations and fear for her physical safety, creating immediate friction between his protectiveness and her need for a private sanctuary.
</plan>
<nar>
Violet's analytical gaze sweeps past the shouting clusters of cadets and the blood-greased benches of {{The Mess Hall|loc}}, tracking the architectural lines of the stone vaulting. 

Her mind, honed by years of studying the structural blueprints of {{Basgiath War College|loc}}, notes an asymmetry in the western load-bearing wall behind the auxiliary service racks. 

When Dain turns for a fraction of a second to accept a heavy wooden tray of rations from a mess server, Violet slips away from his side, her boots making barely a sound against the flagstones as she skirts the edge of the crowded hall.

She traces the damp stone exterior of the barracks until she finds it: a narrow, iron-strapped maintenance door, almost entirely swallowed by thick emerald moss and half-concealed behind a stack of rotting crate timbers. 

There are no official seals upon it, nor any guard posted, which in the lethal hierarchy of the Riders Quadrant means it is either forgotten or strictly forbidden. 

With a quiet heave, Violet tests the heavy iron latch, her fingers biting into the cold metal as the mechanism gives way with a low, grating groan that is entirely swallowed by the surrounding din of the mess hall.

'Let them think I'm hiding in the back rows.'

Inside lies a steep, spiraling stone staircase plunging downward into absolute darkness, carrying the sharp, mineral tang of stagnant dampness and old blood long since scrubbed from the flags. 

Before she can take a single step into the descent, a heavy hand grips her shoulder, spinning her around with enough force to send a sharp, warning jolt through her fragile, braced joints. 

Dain stands there, his expression darkening from mere anxiety into genuine alarm as he looks past her shoulder toward the yawning black stairwell.

"What do you think you're doing, Violet?" Dain demands, his voice dropping into a harsh, controlled whisper as he blocks the threshold with his broad frame. "That's an unmapped sub-level beneath the old sparring cells. Cadets don't go down there unless they want an 'accident' the leadership can write off as routine mortality. Get back to the table."
</nar>

twist: Dain reads her momentary distraction not as historical recall, but as disorientation from physical weakness, and physically steers her away from the door by her uninjured arm.

Violet's gaze unfocuses for a fraction of a second, drifting past Dain's rigid shoulder as her brilliant, analytical mind retreats inward. 

The mental architecture of her late father's secret maps and forbidden texts rises unbidden behind her eyes—she pictures the windswept crags of Zenithal Watch, a remote stone bastion perched days away in the jagged eastern mountains beyond {{Atherbyne|loc|athebyne}}, far beyond the reach of her mother's punitive gaze, where military deserters and the broken remnants of failed squads are whispered to vanish into the mist.

'It's a sanctuary for ghosts.'

Dain catches the sudden stillness in her posture, misinterpreting the intense intellectual focus as physical dizziness or failing strength. 

His hand wraps firmly around her upper arm—careful of her sensitive joints, yet entirely unyielding—and physically pulls her away from the dark threshold, easing the heavy iron-strapped door shut with a muffled, echoing thud.

"Stop letting your mind wander into the archives. <plan>
twist: Dain doesn't just dismiss it as a cadet rumor; he recognizes the name instantly because his father discussed classified border patrols there, locking down his expression with immediate military panic.
distinct: Dain's reaction is driven entirely by his rule-abiding anxiety and his fear of General Sorrengail's wrath, treating any mention of unauthorized border outposts or strange lights as treasonous heresy.

<nar>
Violet lets Dain steer her back toward the crowded rows of tables, but as he pulls out a scarred wooden bench for her, she offers a casual, deceptively innocent prompt. 

"Have you ever heard of Zenithal Watch, Dain?" she asks, lowering her voice just enough to cut through the surrounding din of clattering tin cups and shouting cadets. "The watchtower at Athebyne logged strange lights moving through those eastern peaks three nights ago. Before my mother had the reports scrubbed."

Dain freezes midway through shoving a heavy iron plate of dried bread and salted beef toward her. 

The color drains slightly from his face, and his hands snap flat against the edge of the scarred table, his knuckles whitening as he leans in close, his eyes wide with sudden, sharp alarm.

"Where on earth did you hear that name, Violet?" Dain hisses, his voice dropping into a harsh, frantic whisper that vibrates with tension. 

He casts a rapid, paranoid glance over his shoulder to ensure none of the surrounding second-year squad leaders are paying attention. 

"That sector is classified. My father reviews those patrol logs directly from the General's command staff. There are no lights in the eastern mountains—only dead rock and storms. If anyone hears you talking about unverified patrols or scrubbed reports outside the Scribe archives, they won't just think you're eccentric; they'll think you're leaking intelligence."

He grabs her wrist, his grip firm and protective, though his thumb presses warningly against her pulse point. 

"Drop it, Violet. For your own safety, pretend you never read whatever archival draft put that idea into your head. The war on the borders isn't a history lesson; it's a butcher's bill."
</nar>

raw:
<plan>
twist: the ledger isn't being kept by the scribes in the open anymore; it's already been confiscated by the wingleader's staff, turning a simple archive check into a direct confrontation with someone watching her.
distinct: Dain tries to physically bar her from going back out, arguing that looking at the dead won't bring them back and only draws unwanted attention from second-years who survived crossing.
</plan>
<nar>
Violet pulls her arm from Dain's grip with a quiet, stubborn tug, ignoring the warning flare of pain in her shoulder joint. 

"I need to see the ledger, Dain," she says, her tone flat and unyielding as she stands up from the mess hall bench. "Knowing who fell on the {{The Parapet|loc}} is tactical data, not grief."

Before Dain can block her path or argue further, Violet turns sharply on her heel and pushes her way back through the heavy oak doors of {{The Mess Hall|loc}}, leaving the deafening roar of the cadets behind. 

The midday air outside is crisp, smelling sharply of wet stone and ozone from the open expanse of {{Basgiath War College|loc}}. 

She crosses the quadrangle, her boots clicking against the flagstones as she makes her way toward the administrative stone archway where the official casualty scrolls are traditionally pinned after each trial.

As she approaches the narrow reading desk outside the scribe annex, she finds the parchment board heavily guarded. 

An administrative scribe cadet stands beside the iron spike, frantically rolling up the blood-spattered parchment sheets under the watchful eye of a senior cadre member. 

The death toll from the morning crossing is already staggering, dozens of names slashed through with thick red ink.

Before Violet can step close enough to read the remaining legible entries, a heavy shadow falls across the stone desk. 

{{Xaden Riorson|npc}} steps out from the archway's recess, his black leather uniform immaculate, his scarred face unreadable as his dark eyes lock onto Violet with cool, unnerving precision. 

"Looking for familiar names, Sorrengail?" Xaden asks, his voice low, rich, and dangerously smooth as he leans against the stone pillar, blocking her access to the ledger completely. "Or are you just checking to see how many ghosts you're expected to join before tomorrow's assembly?"
</nar>
